items.quote: Concept 1 · Complex number
items.text: Concept 1 · Complex number

items.quote: When a medical technician monitors a patient's heart
items.text: When a medical technician monitors a patient's heart using an electrocardiogram (ECG), the screen displays a rhythmic, wave-like pattern. Similarly, an MRI machine uses powerful magnetic fields and radio waves to construct detailed images of organs inside the human body. These biological signals are fundamentally waves, and tracking them requires tracking both their size (amplitude) and their timing (phase shift). While standard numbers fail to capture both pieces of data simultaneously, a unique mathematical framework solves this problem perfectly by treating numbers as coordinates on a plane.

items.quote: BIOLOGICAL SIGNALS: WAVES & COMPLEX NUMBERS

items.text: Guiding Question: How can complex numbers help us expand our understanding of mathematics so that we can solve problems that seem impossible using only real numbers?

items.quote: The number whose square is −1 is denoted by i.
items.claim: The number whose square is −1 is denoted by i; that is, i² = −1.

items.quote: A number expressed in the form a + bi using two real numbers a, b is called a complex number.
items.claim: A number expressed in the form a + bi using two real numbers a, b is called a complex number.

items.quote: The part a is called the Real Part, and the part b is called the Imaginary Part.
items.claim: The part a is called the real part, and the part b is called the imaginary part.
items.notes: 'Real Part' and 'Imaginary Part' are printed as red fill-in terms.

items.quote: When b = 0, a + bi becomes a real number.
items.claim: When b = 0, a + bi becomes a real number.

items.quote: When b ≠ 0, a + bi is called an imaginary number.
items.claim: When b ≠ 0, a + bi is called an imaginary number.

items.quote: When a, b, c, d are real numbers, if a + bi = c + di, then
items.claim: Equality of complex numbers: when a, b, c, d are real numbers, if a + bi = c + di, then a = c, b = d.

items.quote: When a, b are real numbers, if a + bi = 0, then a = 0, b = 0
items.claim: When a, b are real numbers, if a + bi = 0, then a = 0, b = 0.

items.quote: A sound engineer is programming a stereo echo plugin
items.text: A sound engineer is programming a stereo echo plugin where complex numbers track the volume and timing of audio waves. To perfectly center the sound between the left speaker (volume multiplier x) and right speaker (volume multiplier y), the two audio paths must balance according to this equation: $(1+2i)(x+i)=x(y+i)$. Find the exact values of the real numbers x and y.
items.notes: A photo of a sound engineer at a mixing screen accompanies the text; treated as decorative.

items.text: Learning Outcomes: Identify the complex number ($z = a + bi$) and its components (the real part and the imaginary part). Perform arithmetic operations (addition, subtraction, multiplication, division) on complex numbers and put them in their simplest form.

items.quote: Calculations involving complex numbers can be performed in the same way as algebraic expressions.
items.claim: Calculations with complex numbers can be performed in the same way as algebraic expressions. However, if i² appears, substitute i² = −1.

items.quote: Powers of i should be calculated by expressing them in terms of i²
items.claim: Powers of i should be calculated by expressing them in terms of i². Example: i⁸ = (i²)⁴ = (−1)⁴ = 1; i⁷ = i × (i²)³ = i × (−1)³ = −i.

items.quote: When the exponent is odd, express it using i and i².
items.text: Side note (attached to the i⁷ example): When the exponent is odd, express it using $i$ and $i^2$.

learning_objectives.label: Parts and equality of complex numbers
learning_objectives.description: Identify the real and imaginary parts of a complex number a + bi (including real numbers and numbers such as 2i) and use equality of complex numbers to find real x and y.

learning_objectives.label: Add, subtract, multiply complex numbers
learning_objectives.description: Calculate sums, differences, products and powers of complex numbers, substituting i² = −1, and give the answer in the form a + bi.

learning_objectives.label: Conjugates and dividing complex numbers
learning_objectives.description: State the complex conjugate of a complex number and divide complex numbers by multiplying numerator and denominator by the conjugate of the denominator, answering in the form a + bi.

learning_objectives.label: Square roots of negative numbers
learning_objectives.description: Express square roots of negative numbers in terms of i and calculate with them.
